newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland, Greece to step up defence cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Poland, Greece to step up defence cooperation.

text.p: Polish and Greek experts will meet soon to draft an agreement on scientific and technological cooperation in the military and defence industry fields, the countries' defence ministers said on Monday.

Greece's minister, Akis Tsohatzopoulos, who met his Polish counterpart, Stanislaw Dobrzanski, during a one-day working visit to Warsaw, reaffirmed support for Poland's bid to join NATO, the western defence alliance to which Greece already belongs.
PAP news agency reported the ministers as telling a joint news conference their countries, which signed an agreement on military cooperation in 1992, planned to increase such links.
In preliminary talks, Greece expressed an interest in the new Huzar combat helicopter being developed in Poland, and in collaboration over maritime technology, the agency said.
Dobrzanski said there was no danger that the Greek parliament would fail to ratify Poland's eagerly sought admission to NATO, which must be approved by all 16 existing member states.
